title: Stream-lockless graph anchor and rollback coordination for preemptible multi-stream decode
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Intermittent corruption and nondeterministic failures have been observed during CUDA Graph capture/replay when a decode spans multiple streams and a preemptible GPU eviction (or scheduler preemption) forces a recapture. This ticket designs and implements a lockless anchor/rollback coordination protocol that ensures safe handoff between streams, deterministic kernel selection on replay, and an auditable capture diff that enables automated rollback without global stalls.
background: Symptoms: occasional mismatched logits after replay, spike in tail-latency during recapture, and rare panics in fused-attention kernels when capture boundaries were inserted mid-prefill. Root causes include: (1) capture starting/stopping on different stream epochs without an agreed anchor, (2) kernel selection heuristics diverging due to sequence-length/inflight batch differences at recapture, and (3) partial KV-cache state leading to non-idempotent replay. Existing mitigations (coarse global mutex around recapture) regress throughput and increase latency for short requests.
proposal: Introduce a lockless 'graph anchor' abstraction per decode cohort: a small 64-bit epoch token and anchor descriptor that is atomically published via an epoch store (lightweight GPU-visible and CPU-visible). Each stream holds an anchor token while capturing; recapture acquires a new token and performs an epoch-verified capture. Add a deterministic kernel-hint serialization into the anchor descriptor so replay chooses the same kernel configuration. For safety, implement a checkpoint-and-compare diff: after capture but before commit, compute a brief capture-checksum over the capture plan and KV-index summary; if checksum mismatches on replay attempts, fall back to software decode or a conservative kernel path. All operations avoid global locks—streams coordinate via epoch tokens and compare-and-swap semantics.
implementation_steps: Design epoch token layout and lightweight epoch store API (GPU and CPU accessible).
Add kernel-hint serialization into capture metadata and store in anchor descriptor.
Implement capture-checksum (captures plan hash + KV-index fingerprint).
Add compare-and-commit protocol: tentative-capture -> checksum-verify -> atomic-publish -> release anchor.
Implement fallback path: software decode or single-stream conservative kernels if checksum fails or anchor publish races.
Extensive unit tests and integration tests including deterministic-seed fuzz harness.
Instrument metrics and tracing for anchor lifecycle, checksum failures, and kernel-hint mismatches.
Create rollout plan and gradual canary (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated rollback triggers.
acceptance_criteria: No regressions in p50/p95 latency on standard decode workloads vs baseline (within 3%).
Replayer checksum mismatches <= 0.01% in stress test; any mismatch triggers safe fallback.
Deterministic replay across 10k seeded fuzz runs (same logits/kv-state or safe fallback logged).
Canaries report no increase in customer-visible errors during 10-day trial at 10% traffic.
Comprehensive tracing exists for anchor lifecycle and is surfaced in Console.
testing_plan: Unit tests for epoch-store CAS semantics and kernel-hint roundtrip.
Deterministic seeded fuzz harness that drives multi-stream prefill+decode with random preemption points.
Cluster-level soak test on preemptible instance fleet for 48 hours measuring checksum/fallback rates.
End-to-end regression test comparing logits and KV-cache state between baseline (no recapture) and new protocol.
Chaos test: inject artificial evictions and stream reorderings to validate lockless coordination.
rollout_plan: Internal canary: 0% -> 1% -> 10% (48h each) measuring fallback and error metrics.
Public canary: 10% for 7 days with automated rollback if replay_fallback_rate > 0.5% or customer_errors increase by > 20% relative to baseline.
Gradual ramp to 50% then 100% with monitoring and on-call readiness.
blockers: Need kernel-hint ABI agreed with fused-attn team (meeting scheduled).
GPU-visible atomic support on some legacy instances is partial; must validate fallback path.
